changeLogMessages: Implemented the Credential Refresh Behavior specification for the AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, SSO, Login, EC2 instance metadata (IMDS), container (HTTP) and Cognito credential providers, and classes derived from them. ProcessAWSCredentials, FederatedAWSCredentials and custom providers, including classes derived directly from RefreshingAWSCredentials or URIBasedRefreshingCredentialHelper, keep their existing refresh behavior unless they override the new protected UsesManagedRefreshLifecycle property. The providers above seal that override, so classes derived from them cannot turn it off.

When a refresh of expired credentials fails, these providers now keep using the cached credentials and contact the credential source again only after a jittered backoff that scales with the time the cached credentials have left: 1 to 10 minutes, and 1 to 1.5 minutes once they have expired, instead of throwing as most providers did before. A request sent with expired cached credentials fails with the service's ExpiredToken error, after the retries the client's retry policy allows, instead of the credential source's error, and after the source recovers, calls can keep failing until the backoff ends. InstanceProfileAWSCredentials previously kept using the cached credentials for 2 more minutes instead. The first fetch, when nothing is cached, still throws if it fails; if it returns credentials that have already expired, they are used and refreshed on the next request for credentials.

The background refresh window of these providers is now chosen from the credential lifetime, measured from the reported expiration: 5 minutes for a lifetime of 20 minutes or less, 15 minutes for less than 90 minutes, and 60 minutes otherwise. SSO, Login and Cognito credentials, which previously refreshed only once they had expired, now refresh in the background too.

A background refresh never starts the interactive SSO sign-in (SsoVerificationCallback or the PKCE flow), whether it refreshes SSOAWSCredentials or a provider, such as AssumeRoleAWSCredentials, whose source credentials they are. When a new SSO token would need it, the cached credentials keep being used and the sign-in starts in the first call that finds them expired, on the caller's thread for a synchronous call. Earlier versions could start it during the background refresh of such a provider.

A PreemptExpiryTime value that is set still takes precedence and applies to credentials fetched after it is set; when it has not been set, reading it on these providers returns the window chosen for the current credentials. Credentials already inside their window when fetched no longer start a background refresh on every call; they are refreshed when a call finds them at their expiration.

When a service rejects a request with ExpiredToken or ExpiredTokenException (the code JSON-protocol services such as DynamoDB and Lambda return) and the request was signed with credentials from one of these providers, the SDK now marks those credentials expired (new RefreshingAWSCredentials.Invalidate method; the new IRequestContext.ResolvedCredentials property records the credentials each request was signed with) and retries the request, signed with credentials resolved again. The retries count toward the maximum attempts and consume retry quota, RetryPolicy.RetryForException does not control them, and MaxErrorRetry = 0 disables them.

Added AmazonNonRecoverableCredentialsException for refresh failures that retrying cannot resolve, such as an expired SSO session or an STS AccessDenied. It derives from AmazonClientException, so existing catch (AmazonClientException) handlers still catch it. Where it replaces the AmazonClientException that earlier versions threw for an STS rejection or a failure of the source credentials of AssumeRole, it has the same message and InnerException; the SSO and Login messages changed, as described below.

A refresh is non-recoverable when an SSO or Login token is missing, malformed, or expired and cannot be refreshed, when the Sign-In service rejects a Login refresh with TOKEN_EXPIRED, USER_CREDENTIALS_CHANGED, INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS or a ValidationException (raised even while the Login token has not expired), or when STS returns AccessDenied, IDPRejectedClaim, InvalidIdentityToken, MalformedPolicyDocument, PackedPolicyTooLarge or RegionDisabled, including for the source credentials of AssumeRole.
The SSO service's UnauthorizedException is also non-recoverable and is raised unchanged. Other refresh failures, such as network errors, throttling and other service errors, stay recoverable.

These providers raise a non-recoverable error immediately, with no refresh backoff and no fallback to cached credentials, and raise it again for 1-5 seconds without contacting the credential source. One raised by a background refresh is raised by the next call, even while the cached credentials are still valid.
SSO and Login errors for a token that is missing, malformed, or expired and cannot be refreshed now end with "Please reauthenticate."; the rest of each existing message is unchanged.

InstanceProfileAWSCredentials no longer extends the expiration of cached credentials or reports a made-up expiry during an IMDS outage. Both EC2 instance metadata providers report the expiration IMDS returned and try IMDS again after the refresh backoff. The default provider still looks for newer credentials every 2 minutes, in a background refresh that never blocks callers, so it picks up the credentials IMDS rotates in and a replaced instance role, as before. InstanceProfileAWSCredentials now does the same while IMDS is enabled, until it is disposed. An already-expired IMDS response does not replace cached credentials. InstanceProfileAWSCredentials still makes a failed request once more when nothing is cached, but after ClearCredentials it no longer falls back to the credentials it had before.

The process-wide instance metadata credentials provider was replaced by one per DefaultAWSCredentialsIdentityResolver instance, one for FallbackCredentialsFactory, and one per resolution of a credential_source=Ec2InstanceMetadata profile, each with its own cache.

RefreshingAWSCredentials.GetCredentials(TimeSpan), which the RDS and DSQL auth token generators and AWSSigV4Signer presigning use, is not limited by the refresh backoff and throws when its refresh fails. The EC2 instance metadata providers do not apply the minimum lifetime, because IMDS cannot supply longer-lived credentials on request: for them it behaves as GetCredentials(). InstanceProfileAWSCredentials previously contacted IMDS when its cached credentials expired within the minimum lifetime.

AssumeRoleWithWebIdentityCredentials now reads the web identity token file again and calls STS again, up to the default retry count, when STS rejects the token as expired, so a token rotated on disk is picked up within the same refresh.

Fixed a defect where a failed background credential refresh could raise TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException. Refresh failures that the SDK handles by using cached credentials are now logged at Warn with the credential source's error, and the use of cached credentials during a refresh backoff is logged once per backoff. ProcessAWSCredentials, FederatedAWSCredentials and other providers still log a failed background refresh at Error.

CognitoAWSCredentials now uses the credential refresh lifecycle in AWSSDK.Core: it refreshes in the background before the credentials expire, and keeps using the cached credentials after a transient refresh failure, trying again after the refresh backoff. NotAuthorizedException, ResourceNotFoundException and InvalidIdentityPoolConfigurationException are non-recoverable and are thrown immediately. A class that overrides only RefreshIdentity, as developer authenticated identities do, now has that override used by the asynchronous methods and the background refresh as well.

AccessDeniedException now reports its OAuth2 error to the Login credential provider in AWSSDK.Core, which treats a refresh rejected with TOKEN_EXPIRED, USER_CREDENTIALS_CHANGED or INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS as non-recoverable. It implements the new Amazon.Runtime.Internal.ICredentialRefreshErrorCode interface from AWSSDK.Core explicitly, so AccessDeniedException gains no public member.
